description: End-to-end algorithm improving local fulfillment rates by 0.54% across millions of weekly orders in two-echelon distribution. Franz Edelman Award finalist.

name: DeepETA: How Uber Predicts Arrival Times Using Deep Learning
title: DeepETA: How Uber Predicts Arrival Times Using Deep Learning
authors: Xinyu Hu, Olcay Cirit, et al.
description: Uber's production ETA using Transformers for tabular data; highest QPS system at Uber.

name: The Effects of Uber's Surge Pricing: A Case Study
title: The Effects of Uber's Surge Pricing: A Case Study
authors: Jonathan Hall, Cory Kendrick, Chris Nosko
description: Natural experiment (NYE outage) showing dynamic pricing equilibrates supply/demand in real-time.

name: Dynamic Pricing in a Labor Market: Surge Pricing and Flexible Work on the Uber Platform
title: Dynamic Pricing in a Labor Market: Surge Pricing and Flexible Work on the Uber Platform
description: Studies driver labor supply response using 25 million Uber trips.

name: Estimating Performance in a Robotic Mobile Fulfillment System
title: Estimating Performance in a Robotic Mobile Fulfillment System
authors: Thibaud Lamballais, Debjit Roy, René de Koster
description: Highly-cited queueing network model for Amazon-style RMFS; foundational for warehouse layout optimization and throughput analysis.

name: RAPPOR: Randomized Aggregatable Privacy-Preserving Ordinal Response
title: RAPPOR: Randomized Aggregatable Privacy-Preserving Ordinal Response
authors: Úlfar Erlingsson, Vasyl Pihur, Aleksandra Korolova
description: Google's practical local DP system deployed in Chrome with longitudinal privacy guarantees.

name: RAPPOR: Randomized Aggregatable Privacy-Preserving Ordinal Response
title: RAPPOR: Randomized Aggregatable Privacy-Preserving Ordinal Response
authors: Úlfar Erlingsson, Vasyl Pihur, Aleksandra Korolova
description: Foundation for privacy-preserving telemetry with local DP guarantees for aggregate statistics.

name: Modeling Tabular Data using Conditional GAN (CTGAN)
title: Modeling Tabular Data using Conditional GAN (CTGAN)
authors: Lei Xu, Maria Skoularidou, Alfredo Cuesta-Infante, Kalyan Veeramachaneni
description: State-of-the-art GAN for synthetic tabular data; handles mixed types with mode-specific normalization.

name: Robust De-anonymization of Large Sparse Datasets (Netflix)
title: Robust De-anonymization of Large Sparse Datasets (Netflix)
description: Landmark attack demonstrating re-identification of Netflix users; showed k-anonymity fails on high-dimensional data.

name: t-Closeness: Privacy Beyond k-Anonymity and ℓ-Diversity
title: t-Closeness: Privacy Beyond k-Anonymity and ℓ-Diversity
authors: Ninghui Li, Tiancheng Li, Suresh Venkatasubramanian
description: Requires sensitive attribute distribution in each equivalence class be close to overall distribution.

name: Deep Gravity: Large-Scale Origin-Destination Flows
title: Deep Gravity: Large-Scale Origin-Destination Flows
description: Neural network predicting mobility flows, outperforming classic gravity models.

name: Understanding Uber Demand
title: Understanding Uber Demand
description: Uber's real-time geospatial demand prediction powering surge and dispatch.

name: Starbucks Store Locator with Machine Learning
title: Starbucks Store Locator with Machine Learning
description: ML-driven site selection combining foot traffic, demographics, and competition.
category: Spatial & Geo > Location Choice & Site Selection

name: Spatial Spillovers in Airbnb Pricing
title: Spatial Spillovers in Airbnb Pricing
authors: Nils Kok, Edward Kopczuk, Maisy Wong
description: Demonstrates spatial lag effects in short-term rental markets using hedonic models.

name: libpostal: International Address Parsing
title: libpostal: International Address Parsing
description: NLP library parsing addresses in 60+ languages—widely used in ride-sharing and logistics.

name: H3: Uber's Hexagonal Hierarchical Spatial Index
title: H3: Uber's Hexagonal Hierarchical Spatial Index
description: Hexagonal grid system enabling efficient geospatial joins and aggregations.

name: Placekey: A Universal Place Identifier
title: Placekey: A Universal Place Identifier
description: Standardized POI identifier joining disparate datasets without address matching.

name: Google Mobility Reports
title: Google Mobility Reports
description: Aggregated mobility trends by place category—used globally for pandemic response.

name: SafeGraph Foot Traffic Data
title: SafeGraph Foot Traffic Data
description: Panel-based POI visit data enabling offline-to-online attribution and demand studies.

name: The Market for 'Lemons': Quality Uncertainty and the Market Mechanism
title: The Market for 'Lemons': Quality Uncertainty and the Market Mechanism
description: Nobel Prize-winning paper introducing asymmetric information theory. Though focused on used cars, it explains why 'bad risks' can drive out good risks in insurance markets, establishing the intellectual foundation for adverse selection analysis.
category: Insurtech & Insurance Economics > Foundational Insurance Economics

name: Equilibrium in Competitive Insurance Markets: An Essay on the Economics of Imperfect Information
title: Equilibrium in Competitive Insurance Markets: An Essay on the Economics of Imperfect Information
description: The most-cited paper in insurance economics. Demonstrates how insurers design contracts to induce self-selection by risk types and proves that pooling equilibria cannot survive competition. Nobel Prize work.
category: Insurtech & Insurance Economics > Foundational Insurance Economics

name: Uncertainty and the Welfare Economics of Medical Care
title: Uncertainty and the Welfare Economics of Medical Care
description: The founding paper of health economics. Analyzes the special characteristics of medical care markets and introduces moral hazard as a fundamental problem in health insurance.
category: Insurtech & Insurance Economics > Foundational Insurance Economics

name: Testing for Asymmetric Information in Insurance Markets
title: Testing for Asymmetric Information in Insurance Markets
description: Introduced the conditional correlation test now standard across the field for detecting asymmetric information. Using French auto insurance data, found no evidence for asymmetric information in that market.
category: Insurtech & Insurance Economics > Foundational Insurance Economics

name: Multiple Dimensions of Private Information: Evidence from the Long-Term Care Insurance Market
title: Multiple Dimensions of Private Information: Evidence from the Long-Term Care Insurance Market
description: Showed that private information operates on multiple dimensions—risk AND preferences—explaining puzzling cases where riskier individuals don't always buy more coverage.
category: Insurtech & Insurance Economics > Foundational Insurance Economics

name: Health Insurance and the Demand for Medical Care: Evidence from a Randomized Experiment
title: Health Insurance and the Demand for Medical Care: Evidence from a Randomized Experiment
description: The RAND Health Insurance Experiment—gold-standard randomized evidence showing price elasticity of healthcare demand around -0.2, meaning cost-sharing reduces utilization by 25-30%.
category: Insurtech & Insurance Economics > Foundational Insurance Economics

name: Equilibrium in a Reinsurance Market
title: Equilibrium in a Reinsurance Market
description: Foundational paper for understanding risk-sharing and reinsurance. Introduced conditions for Pareto-optimal risk allocation and the concept of companies trading risk as a commodity.
category: Insurtech & Insurance Economics > Foundational Insurance Economics

name: Machine Learning in P&C Insurance: A Review for Pricing and Reserving
title: Machine Learning in P&C Insurance: A Review for Pricing and Reserving
authors: Christopher Blier-Wong, Hélène Cossette, Luc Lamontagne, Etienne Marceau
description: Comprehensive review synthesizing ~100 articles on ML in property and casualty insurance. Documents the evolution from GLMs to gradient boosted machines and neural networks.
category: Insurtech & Insurance Economics > Machine Learning for Insurance Pricing

name: From Generalized Linear Models to Neural Networks, and Back
title: From Generalized Linear Models to Neural Networks, and Back
description: Demonstrates the mathematical connections between traditional actuarial methods and deep learning, enabling practitioners to blend actuarial intuition with ML flexibility. Introduces the CANN approach.
category: Insurtech & Insurance Economics > Machine Learning for Insurance Pricing

name: DeepTriangle: A Deep Learning Approach to Loss Reserving
title: DeepTriangle: A Deep Learning Approach to Loss Reserving
description: Introduced RNN architectures for joint prediction of paid and outstanding claims. Uses gated recurrent units to process loss triangles, improving on traditional stochastic reserving methods.
category: Insurtech & Insurance Economics > Machine Learning for Insurance Pricing

name: The Impact of Digitalization on the Insurance Value Chain and the Insurability of Risks
title: The Impact of Digitalization on the Insurance Value Chain and the Insurability of Risks
description: Highly-cited analysis of 84 studies through Porter's value chain lens. Identifies four major industry tasks: enhancing customer experience, improving processes, offering new products, and preparing for cross-industry competition.
category: Insurtech & Insurance Economics > InsurTech & Digital Transformation

name: The Baseball Players' Labor Market
title: The Baseball Players' Labor Market
description: THE birth certificate of sports economics. Introduced the Invariance Principle (predating Coase's Theorem) showing talent allocation would be identical under free agency or the reserve clause. Also articulated the Uncertainty of Outcome Hypothesis: competitive balance matters for fan interest.
category: Sports Economics & Analytics > Player Labor Markets & Team Economics

name: Pay and Performance in Major League Baseball
title: Pay and Performance in Major League Baseball
description: Pioneered empirical estimation of player marginal revenue product (MRP). Using two-stage regression (performance→wins→revenue), demonstrated players earned just 10-20% of their MRP under the reserve clause—empirical ammunition for free agency litigation.
category: Sports Economics & Analytics > Player Labor Markets & Team Economics

name: Cross-Subsidization, Incentives, and Outcomes in Professional Team Sports Leagues
title: Cross-Subsidization, Incentives, and Outcomes in Professional Team Sports Leagues
description: Synthesized 40 years of sports economics research into the definitive framework. Striking finding: revenue sharing generally has no impact on competitive balance (reinforcing Rottenberg's invariance), though salary caps do affect balance.
category: Sports Economics & Analytics > Player Labor Markets & Team Economics

name: The Loser's Curse: Decision Making and Market Efficiency in the National Football League Draft
title: The Loser's Curse: Decision Making and Market Efficiency in the National Football League Draft
description: Demonstrated NFL draft picks are systematically overvalued. Top picks generate less surplus value than late first-rounders, teams exhibit overconfidence and the winner's curse. Implied discount rate in multi-year trades reached 136%. Influenced teams like New England to trade down systematically.
category: Sports Economics & Analytics > Player Labor Markets & Team Economics

name: Professionals Play Minimax
title: Professionals Play Minimax
description: Analyzed 1,417 penalty kicks from top European leagues. Kickers and goalkeepers play exactly according to mixed-strategy Nash equilibrium: success probabilities are statistically identical across strategies, and choices show true serial independence. First field support for both implications of von Neumann's Minimax Theorem.
category: Sports Economics & Analytics > Game Theory & Strategic Behavior in Sports
subtopic: Game Theory & Strategic Behavior in Sports

name: Minimax Play at Wimbledon
title: Minimax Play at Wimbledon
description: Confirmed equilibrium behavior in tennis serves using championship matches featuring McEnroe, Borg, Becker, and Sampras. The same statistical tests that soundly reject equilibrium play in experimental data confirm equilibrium behavior among elite professionals.
category: Sports Economics & Analytics > Game Theory & Strategic Behavior in Sports
subtopic: Game Theory & Strategic Behavior in Sports

name: Expertise, Gender, and Equilibrium Play
title: Expertise, Gender, and Equilibrium Play
authors: Romain Gauriot, Lionel Page, John Wooders
description: Extended minimax analysis to nearly 500,000 serves across 3,000 matches. Found higher-ranked players conform more closely to equilibrium theory, and substantial differences in degree to which men and women conform to equilibrium predictions.
category: Sports Economics & Analytics > Game Theory & Strategic Behavior in Sports
subtopic: Game Theory & Strategic Behavior in Sports

name: Professionals Do Not Play Minimax: Evidence from Major League Baseball and the National Football League
title: Professionals Do Not Play Minimax: Evidence from Major League Baseball and the National Football League
description: Found minimax violations in baseball pitch selection and football play-calling. Pitchers throw too many fastballs; football teams pass less than they should. Suggests the strategic simplicity of penalty kicks and tennis serves may be key to equilibrium play.
category: Sports Economics & Analytics > Game Theory & Strategic Behavior in Sports
subtopic: Game Theory & Strategic Behavior in Sports

name: Anomalies: Parimutuel Betting Markets: Racetracks and Lotteries
title: Anomalies: Parimutuel Betting Markets: Racetracks and Lotteries
authors: Richard H. Thaler, William T. Ziemba
description: Established betting markets as legitimate venues for testing rationality. Despite quick feedback that should facilitate learning, the favorite-longshot bias persists—bettors systematically overweight longshots.
category: Sports Economics & Analytics > Sports Betting & Prediction Markets

name: Explaining the Favorite-Longshot Bias: Is it Risk-Love or Misperceptions?
title: Explaining the Favorite-Longshot Bias: Is it Risk-Love or Misperceptions?
description: Used 5.6 million horse race starts and exotic bet pricing to discriminate between competing theories. Evidence favors probability misperceptions (prospect theory) over risk-love: longshots return about -61% while favorites return approximately -5%.
category: Sports Economics & Analytics > Sports Betting & Prediction Markets

name: Why Are Gambling Markets Organised So Differently from Financial Markets?
title: Why Are Gambling Markets Organised So Differently from Financial Markets?
description: Explains why bookmakers set prices rather than equilibrating supply and demand. Bookmakers are more skilled at predicting outcomes than bettors and systematically exploit bettor biases by choosing prices that deviate from market clearing.
category: Sports Economics & Analytics > Sports Betting & Prediction Markets

name: An Economic Model of a Professional Sports League
title: An Economic Model of a Professional Sports League
description: First mathematically rigorous league model. Key finding: equalization of playing strengths is inconsistent with profit maximization under standard rules—challenged assumptions about natural competitive balance.
category: Sports Economics & Analytics > Sports Analytics Methods

name: Rank-Order Tournaments as Optimum Labor Contracts
title: Rank-Order Tournaments as Optimum Labor Contracts
description: Provides the theoretical foundation for understanding prize structures in sports. Key predictions: effort increases with the spread between winning and losing prizes, and only the difference matters, not absolute prize sizes. Introduced competitive handicapping for efficient competition among heterogeneous abilities.
category: Sports Economics & Analytics > Sports Analytics Methods

name: The Economic Design of Sporting Contests
title: The Economic Design of Sporting Contests
description: Comprehensive review covering optimal prize structures, incentive-balance tradeoffs, and revenue sharing effects. Draws together research on individualistic sports (golf, footraces) with team sports (baseball, soccer) through the lens of contest theory.
category: Sports Economics & Analytics > Sports Analytics Methods

name: Do Firms Maximize? Evidence from Professional Football
title: Do Firms Maximize? Evidence from Professional Football
description: Used dynamic programming to show NFL teams punt and kick field goals far too often. Going for a touchdown from the opponent's 2-yard line instead of taking the field goal increases win probability by approximately 3%. Originally titled 'It's Fourth Down and What Does the Bellman Equation Say?'
category: Sports Economics & Analytics > Sports Analytics Methods

name: A Multiresolution Stochastic Process Model for Predicting Basketball Possession Outcomes
title: A Multiresolution Stochastic Process Model for Predicting Basketball Possession Outcomes
authors: Daniel Cervone, Alexander D'Amour, Luke Bornn, Kirk Goldsberry
description: Introduced Expected Possession Value (EPV) using player tracking data—the foundation for real-time decision valuation in basketball. Models possessions at multiple resolution levels, differentiating continuous player movements from discrete events like shots and turnovers.
category: Sports Economics & Analytics > Sports Analytics Methods

name: Congestion Theory and Transport Investment
title: Congestion Theory and Transport Investment
description: Nobel Prize-winning bottleneck model showing optimal time-varying tolls can eliminate queuing waste. The birth certificate of dynamic congestion pricing.
category: Transportation Economics & Technology > Congestion Pricing Theory

name: The Scheduling of Consumer Activities: Work Trips
title: The Scheduling of Consumer Activities: Work Trips
description: Established the α-β-γ framework for empirically estimating schedule delay costs. The standard methodology for valuing time in transportation.
category: Transportation Economics & Technology > Congestion Pricing Theory

name: Valuing Time and Reliability: Assessing the Evidence from Road Pricing Demonstrations
title: Valuing Time and Reliability: Assessing the Evidence from Road Pricing Demonstrations
description: Synthesized revealed-preference estimates of value of time from California toll road experiments. Found VOT around 50% of wage rate with substantial heterogeneity.
category: Transportation Economics & Technology > Mode Choice & Discrete Choice

name: Optimization and Scale Economies in Urban Bus Transportation
title: Optimization and Scale Economies in Urban Bus Transportation
description: Established the Mohring Effect: as ridership increases, higher frequency reduces waiting time, creating user-side scale economies that justify transit subsidies.

name: Should Urban Transit Subsidies Be Reduced?
title: Should Urban Transit Subsidies Be Reduced?
description: Derived empirically tractable formulas for optimal transit subsidies accounting for congestion, pollution, accident externalities, and scale economies. Found large fare subsidies typically welfare-improving.

name: The Theory and Measurement of Private and Social Cost of Highway Congestion
title: The Theory and Measurement of Private and Social Cost of Highway Congestion
description: Developed speed-flow relationships for optimal congestion charges. Showed efficient prices far exceed gasoline taxes—foundational for road pricing economics.

name: Disruptive Change in the Taxi Business: The Case of Uber
title: Disruptive Change in the Taxi Business: The Case of Uber
description: Found UberX drivers have 30-50% higher capacity utilization than taxis due to more efficient matching through the platform.
category: Transportation Economics & Technology > Ridesharing & Platform Economics

name: Air Travel Demand and Airline Seat Inventory Management
title: Air Travel Demand and Airline Seat Inventory Management
description: Introduced the Expected Marginal Seat Revenue (EMSR) decision model—foundational for airline revenue management practice.

name: Competition and Price Dispersion in the U.S. Airline Industry
title: Competition and Price Dispersion in the U.S. Airline Industry
description: Found the expected absolute difference in fares between passengers averages 36% of ticket price, with dispersion increasing under competition.

name: Hubs and High Fares: Dominance and Market Power in the U.S. Airline Industry
title: Hubs and High Fares: Dominance and Market Power in the U.S. Airline Industry
description: Documented hub premiums and market power at dominant airports. Showed airlines can charge 10-20% higher fares on routes where they dominate.

name: How Airlines Markets Work...Or Do They? Regulatory Reform in the Airline Industry
title: How Airlines Markets Work...Or Do They? Regulatory Reform in the Airline Industry
description: Found incumbents cut fares significantly when Southwest merely threatens entry, before actual competition begins. Evidence for contestability theory.

name: Carbon Taxes and CO2 Emissions: Sweden as a Case Study
title: Carbon Taxes and CO2 Emissions: Sweden as a Case Study
description: First quasi-experimental study of carbon taxes. Found Sweden's transport CO2 declined ~11% after implementation, with carbon tax elasticity 3x larger than price elasticity.
category: Transportation Economics & Technology > Environmental & Policy Economics

name: Automobile Externalities and Policies
title: Automobile Externalities and Policies
authors: Ian Parry, Margaret Walls, Winston Harrington
description: Comprehensive review of auto externalities—congestion, accidents, local pollution, and climate. Estimated costs per mile and evaluated policy alternatives.
category: Transportation Economics & Technology > Environmental & Policy Economics

name: E-ZTax: Tax Salience and Tax Rates
title: E-ZTax: Tax Salience and Tax Rates
description: Used electronic toll collection adoption to show reduced tax salience leads to higher toll rates. Pioneering evidence on how payment visibility affects policy outcomes.
category: Transportation Economics & Technology > Environmental & Policy Economics

name: Electric Vehicle Adoption: Effects of Income and Purchase Subsidies
title: Electric Vehicle Adoption: Effects of Income and Purchase Subsidies
description: Exploited California subsidy variation. Found EV demand is price-elastic (-3.3) with near 100% pass-through. Estimated $12-18 billion needed to reach 1.5 million EVs.
category: Transportation Economics & Technology > Environmental & Policy Economics

name: Preparing a Nation for Autonomous Vehicles: Opportunities, Barriers and Policy Recommendations
title: Preparing a Nation for Autonomous Vehicles: Opportunities, Barriers and Policy Recommendations

category: Transportation Economics & Technology > Autonomous Vehicles & Future Mobility

name: Cost and Energy Impacts of Automated Vehicles
title: Cost and Energy Impacts of Automated Vehicles
authors: Patrick Bösch, Felix Becker, Henrik Becker, Kay Axhausen
description: Found shared AVs could be cost-competitive with private car ownership at $0.20-0.50/km, potentially transforming urban mobility economics.

name: Willingness to Pay for Self-Driving Vehicles: Public Interest and Policy Implications
title: Willingness to Pay for Self-Driving Vehicles: Public Interest and Policy Implications
authors: Ricardo Daziano, Mauricio Sarrias, Benjamin Leard
description: Estimated willingness-to-pay for full automation at $4,900 using advanced discrete choice methods, with substantial heterogeneity across consumers.

name: The Political Economy of NATO
title: The Political Economy of NATO
description: Synthesizes how joint products, technology changes, and publicness affect alliance burden-sharing dynamics. Essential reading on NATO economics.

name: Arms and Insecurity
title: Arms and Insecurity

category: Defense & Security Tech Economics > Classic Defense Economics

name: Strategic Missile Equations and the Allocation of Resources
title: Strategic Missile Equations and the Allocation of Resources
description: Shows how Richardson-type equations emerge from rational optimization under nuclear deterrence scenarios. Bridge between formal modeling and strategic analysis.
category: Defense & Security Tech Economics > Classic Defense Economics

name: Sources of Weapon System Cost Growth
title: Sources of Weapon System Cost Growth
authors: Joseph G. Bolten, Robert S. Leonard, Mark V. Arena, Obaid Younossi, Jerry M. Sollinger

name: Why Has the Cost of Navy Ships Risen?
title: Why Has the Cost of Navy Ships Risen?
authors: Mark V. Arena, Irv Blickstein, Obaid Younossi, Clifford A. Grammich
description: Documents Augustine's Law phenomena in shipbuilding—systematic cost growth exceeding inflation due to increasing complexity in naval vessels.
category: Defense & Security Tech Economics > Defense Procurement & Costs

name: The Weapons Acquisition Process: Economic Incentives
title: The Weapons Acquisition Process: Economic Incentives
description: Classic study of how contract types shape contractor behavior in defense acquisition. Foundation for understanding procurement incentives.
category: Defense & Security Tech Economics > Defense Procurement & Costs

name: The Macroeconomic Impact of Defense Industry Consolidation
title: The Macroeconomic Impact of Defense Industry Consolidation
description: Found defense industry consolidation increased use of cost-plus contracts and reduced competitive bidding, though government buyer power constrained cost increases.
category: Defense & Security Tech Economics > Defense Procurement & Costs

name: Quandaries in the Economics of Dual Technologies
title: Quandaries in the Economics of Dual Technologies
description: Analyzes conditions under which military R&D generates civilian benefits, highlighting measurement challenges in dual-use technology spillovers.
category: Defense & Security Tech Economics > Defense Procurement & Costs

name: Research and Development Funding and the Changing Structure of the Tech Industry
title: Research and Development Funding and the Changing Structure of the Tech Industry
authors: Pierre Azoulay, Erica Fuchs, Anna Goldstein, Michael Kearney
description: Identifies when ARPA-style funding works: mission orientation, nascent S-curve technologies, and market frictions justifying government intervention.
category: Defense & Security Tech Economics > Defense Procurement & Costs

name: Why Information Security is Hard—An Economic Perspective
title: Why Information Security is Hard—An Economic Perspective
description: Founded security economics by arguing information insecurity stems from perverse economic incentives, not just technical failures. Introduced network externalities, asymmetric information, and moral hazard in security contexts.
category: Defense & Security Tech Economics > Cybersecurity Economics

name: The Economics of Information Security Investment
title: The Economics of Information Security Investment
authors: Lawrence A. Gordon and Martin P. Loeb
description: The Gordon-Loeb Model: organizations should invest no more than 37% of expected loss from a breach, and investing in moderately vulnerable systems may yield higher returns.
category: Defense & Security Tech Economics > Cybersecurity Economics

name: System Reliability and Free Riding
title: System Reliability and Free Riding
description: Analyzed 'weakest link' versus 'best shot' security models, showing how network structure affects optimal investment strategies.
category: Defense & Security Tech Economics > Cybersecurity Economics

name: Interdependent Security
title: Interdependent Security
description: Game-theoretic foundations for understanding why firms systematically underinvest when security decisions create externalities.
category: Defense & Security Tech Economics > Cybersecurity Economics

name: Insurability of Cyber Risk: An Empirical Analysis
title: Insurability of Cyber Risk: An Empirical Analysis
authors: Christian Biener, Martin Eling, and Jan Hendrik Wirfs
description: Winner of the Shin Research Excellence Award. Extracted 994 cyber loss cases identifying heavy tails, correlated risks, and information asymmetries as key barriers to sustainable cyber insurance markets.
category: Defense & Security Tech Economics > Cybersecurity Economics

name: Cyber Risk, Market Failures, and Financial Stability
title: Cyber Risk, Market Failures, and Financial Stability
authors: Emanuel Kopp, Lincoln Kaffenberger, and Christopher Wilson
description: IMF analysis of cyber risk market failures and financial stability implications, providing policy recommendations for systemic risk management.
category: Defense & Security Tech Economics > Cybersecurity Economics

name: An Empirical Analysis of the Welfare Effects of Vulnerability Disclosure
title: An Empirical Analysis of the Welfare Effects of Vulnerability Disclosure
authors: Ashish Arora, Rahul Telang, and Hao Xu
description: Found public disclosure speeds vendor patch response compared to private disclosure, though attacks increase temporarily. Seminal WEIS paper on disclosure economics.
category: Defense & Security Tech Economics > Cybersecurity Economics

name: Space, the Final Economic Frontier
title: Space, the Final Economic Frontier
description: Brought space economics to mainstream economics attention in JEP, analyzing the shift from government to commercial priorities in a sector now exceeding $300 billion annually.
category: Defense & Security Tech Economics > Space Economics

name: The Recent Large Reduction in Space Launch Cost
title: The Recent Large Reduction in Space Launch Cost
description: NASA technical analysis documenting transformative 20x reduction in LEO launch costs: Space Shuttle $54,500/kg versus Falcon 9 $2,720/kg.
category: Defense & Security Tech Economics > Space Economics

name: Orbital-Use Fees Could More Than Quadruple the Value of the Space Industry
title: Orbital-Use Fees Could More Than Quadruple the Value of the Space Industry
authors: Akhil Rao, Matthew Burgess, and Daniel Kaffine
description: PNAS paper showing imperfect competition among satellite constellations reduces welfare from orbit use by up to 12%—approximately $1.1 billion per year—using a coupled physico-economic model.
category: Defense & Security Tech Economics > Space Economics

name: Ordering the Cosmos: Private Law and Celestial Property Rights
title: Ordering the Cosmos: Private Law and Celestial Property Rights
description: Examines space debris through law and economics frameworks, noting China (42%), US (27.5%), and Russia (25.5%) bear primary responsibility for existing debris.
category: Defense & Security Tech Economics > Space Economics

name: Economic Benefits of the Global Positioning System (GPS)
title: Economic Benefits of the Global Positioning System (GPS)
description: NIST-commissioned study estimating a 30-day GPS outage would cost $1 billion per day, with GPS contributing to 13 of 16 critical infrastructure sectors.
category: Defense & Security Tech Economics > Space Economics

name: The Economics of Space Debris: A Model of Orbital Sustainability
title: The Economics of Space Debris: A Model of Orbital Sustainability
description: Projects debris costs could exceed 0.5% of world GDP long-term without intervention, using integrated assessment modeling for orbital sustainability.
category: Defense & Security Tech Economics > Space Economics

name: The Economics of Russian Drone Warfare
title: The Economics of Russian Drone Warfare
description: Analysis of Russian drone strikes finding Shahed drones cost approximately $35,000 each—with less than 10% hit rates, they represent the most cost-effective munition. When $3 million missiles target $200 drones, the 15,000:1 cost disadvantage threatens traditional air defense economics.
category: Defense & Security Tech Economics > Autonomous Systems Economics

name: Looking Back to Look Forward: Autonomous Systems in Military History
title: Looking Back to Look Forward: Autonomous Systems in Military History
description: Argues autonomy should optimize political and economic cost rather than just tactical characteristics. Autonomous systems work best as cost-saving complements to manned missions.
category: Defense & Security Tech Economics > Autonomous Systems Economics

name: Losing Humanity: The Case Against Killer Robots
title: Losing Humanity: The Case Against Killer Robots
description: Introduced the human-in-the-loop, human-on-the-loop, and human-out-of-the-loop framework now standard in lethal autonomous weapons system (LAWS) policy discussions.
category: Defense & Security Tech Economics > Autonomous Systems Economics

name: Military Applications of Artificial Intelligence
title: Military Applications of Artificial Intelligence
description: Comprehensive RAND assessment comparing U.S., China, and Russia military AI development efforts, with implications for strategic competition.
category: Defense & Security Tech Economics > Autonomous Systems Economics

name: Targeting the Computer: Government Support and International Competition
title: Targeting the Computer: Government Support and International Competition
description: Brookings study documenting the massive role of military procurement in creating U.S. technological leadership in computing.
category: Defense & Security Tech Economics > Autonomous Systems Economics

name: Code, Command, and Conflict: The Economics of Military AI
title: Code, Command, and Conflict: The Economics of Military AI
authors: Belfer Center for Science and International Affairs
description: Documents global military AI spending doubling from $4.6B to $9.2B (2022-2023), projected to reach $38.8B by 2028. Analyzes Project Maven's evolution and private sector dependencies.
category: Defense & Security Tech Economics > Emerging Defense Technologies

name: Post-Quantum Cryptography Standards
title: Post-Quantum Cryptography Standards
description: Finalization of post-quantum cryptography standards (FIPS 203, 204, 205) after eight years of global evaluation. Selected from 82 algorithms submitted by 25 countries.
category: Defense & Security Tech Economics > Emerging Defense Technologies

name: AI Failures and Their Strategic Consequences
title: AI Failures and Their Strategic Consequences
description: Addresses AI system failures and their interaction with strategic factors, recommending approaches to reduce failure likelihood and contain consequences.
category: Defense & Security Tech Economics > Emerging Defense Technologies

name: GPS Vulnerability and Resilient PNT
title: GPS Vulnerability and Resilient PNT

category: Defense & Security Tech Economics > Emerging Defense Technologies

name: Commercial National Security Algorithm Suite 2.0 Transition
title: Commercial National Security Algorithm Suite 2.0 Transition
description: Addresses the 'harvest now, decrypt later' threat that makes current encrypted data potentially vulnerable to future quantum computers, with transition timeline guidance.
category: Defense & Security Tech Economics > Emerging Defense Technologies

name: Optimal Advertising and Optimal Quality
title: Optimal Advertising and Optimal Quality

category: Ad Tech & Digital Advertising Economics > Advertising Economics Foundations

name: Advertising as Information
title: Advertising as Information

name: Price and Advertising Signals of Product Quality
title: Price and Advertising Signals of Product Quality

category: Ad Tech & Digital Advertising Economics > Advertising Economics Foundations

name: The Economics of Information
title: The Economics of Information
description: Nobel Prize-winning work on consumer search theory showing why price dispersion persists even in competitive markets with positive search costs.
category: Ad Tech & Digital Advertising Economics > Advertising Economics Foundations

name: Behavioral Inattention
title: Behavioral Inattention
description: Comprehensive survey synthesizing decades of research on how consumers allocate limited attention—the foundation of attention economics.
category: Ad Tech & Digital Advertising Economics > Advertising Economics Foundations

title: Position Auctions with Consumer Search

name: A Comparison of Approaches to Advertising Measurement
title: A Comparison of Approaches to Advertising Measurement

name: Counterfactual Shapley Values for Multi-Touch Attribution
title: Counterfactual Shapley Values for Multi-Touch Attribution

name: Attribution and the Effectiveness of Online Advertising
title: Attribution and the Effectiveness of Online Advertising
authors: Vibhanshu Abhishek, Stylianos Despotakis, and Raghuram Ravi

category: Ad Tech & Digital Advertising Economics > Measuring Advertising Effects

name: GeoLift: Geo-Experimental Inference with Augmented Synthetic Control
title: GeoLift: Geo-Experimental Inference with Augmented Synthetic Control

category: Ad Tech & Digital Advertising Economics > Measuring Advertising Effects

name: The Economic Value of Cookies

name: Paying for Privacy: The Economic Cost of Third-Party Tracking Restrictions
title: Paying for Privacy: The Economic Cost of Third-Party Tracking Restrictions

description: Large Meta experiment with 70K+ advertisers: median cost per incremental customer rose 31% (from $38.16 to $49.93) without offsite data.
category: Ad Tech & Digital Advertising Economics > Privacy Economics & Targeting

name: The Effects of Privacy Regulation on Advertising
title: The Effects of Privacy Regulation on Advertising

name: Privacy and the Market for Products: Economic Consequences of GDPR
title: Privacy and the Market for Products: Economic Consequences of GDPR

name: The Effect of App Tracking Transparency on Advertising Revenue
title: The Effect of App Tracking Transparency on Advertising Revenue

name: The Impact of iOS Privacy Changes on Advertising
title: The Impact of iOS Privacy Changes on Advertising
authors: Guy Aridor, Yeon-Koo Che, and Tobias Salz
description: Finds conversion-optimized Meta ads showed 37% CTR reduction post-ATT, with smaller firms facing steeper declines in new customer acquisition.
category: Ad Tech & Digital Advertising Economics > Privacy Economics & Targeting

name: The Competitive Effects of Google's Ad Tech Stack
title: The Competitive Effects of Google's Ad Tech Stack

title: Header Bidding and the Competition for Advertising Space

category: Ad Tech & Digital Advertising Economics > Ad Tech Market Structure & Fraud

name: A Model of Ad-Supported Platforms and Click Fraud
title: A Model of Ad-Supported Platforms and Click Fraud
authors: Kenneth C. Wilbur and Yi Zhu
description: Shows conditions under which search engines may allow fraud, formalizing the economics of click fraud in ad-supported platforms.
category: Ad Tech & Digital Advertising Economics > Ad Tech Market Structure & Fraud

name: Mobile Advertising Fraud: Empirical Patterns and Detection Strategies
title: Mobile Advertising Fraud: Empirical Patterns and Detection Strategies
authors: Jian Li, Yuqing Zhang, and Wei Liu
description: First large-scale empirical documentation of mobile ad fraud patterns, identifying concealment strategies in daily traffic patterns.

name: Market Power and Welfare in Asymmetric Divisible Good Auctions
title: Market Power and Welfare in Asymmetric Divisible Good Auctions

title: ANA Programmatic Media Supply Chain Transparency Study

name: Practical Lessons from Predicting Clicks on Ads at Facebook
title: Practical Lessons from Predicting Clicks on Ads at Facebook

description: Facebook's influential paper on CTR prediction combining decision trees with logistic regression, establishing key industrial practices.

name: Real-Time Bidding Algorithms for Performance-Based Display Ad Allocation
title: Real-Time Bidding Algorithms for Performance-Based Display Ad Allocation

description: Formulates RTB as constrained optimization with budget pacing, establishing theoretical foundation for DSP bidding algorithms.

name: Customer Lifetime Value: Marketing Models and Applications
title: Customer Lifetime Value: Marketing Models and Applications

name: On the Profitability of Long-Life Customers in a Noncontractual Setting
title: On the Profitability of Long-Life Customers in a Noncontractual Setting

category: MarTech & Customer Analytics Economics > Customer Lifetime Value Foundations

name: A Customer Lifetime Value Framework for Customer Selection and Resource Allocation Strategy
title: A Customer Lifetime Value Framework for Customer Selection and Resource Allocation Strategy

name: Counting Your Customers the Easy Way: An Alternative to the Pareto/NBD Model
title: Counting Your Customers the Easy Way: An Alternative to the Pareto/NBD Model

description: Develops the BG/NBD (Beta-Geometric/Negative Binomial Distribution) model—vastly easier to implement than Pareto/NBD while achieving similar predictive accuracy. The workhorse model for non-contractual CLV estimation.

name: RFM and CLV: Using Iso-Value Curves for Customer Base Analysis
title: RFM and CLV: Using Iso-Value Curves for Customer Base Analysis

name: Probability Models for Customer-Base Analysis

title: A Note on Deriving the Pareto/NBD Model and Related Expressions

name: Using Collaborative Filtering to Weave an Information Tapestry

name: GroupLens: An Open Architecture for Collaborative Filtering of Netnews
title: GroupLens: An Open Architecture for Collaborative Filtering of Netnews

name: Item-Based Collaborative Filtering Recommendation Algorithms
title: Item-Based Collaborative Filtering Recommendation Algorithms
authors: Badrul Sarwar, George Karypis, Joseph Konstan, John Riedl

name: Hybrid Recommender Systems: Survey and Experiments
title: Hybrid Recommender Systems: Survey and Experiments

category: MarTech & Customer Analytics Economics > Recommendation Systems

name: Retention Futility: Targeting High-Risk Customers Might Be Ineffective
title: Retention Futility: Targeting High-Risk Customers Might Be Ineffective

name: Predicting Customer Lifetime Duration and Future Purchase Behavior
title: Predicting Customer Lifetime Duration and Future Purchase Behavior
authors: Greg M. Allenby, Robert P. Leone, Lichung Jen

title: Bagging and Boosting Classification Trees to Predict Churn

name: A Generalized Framework for Estimating Customer Lifetime Value When Customer Lifetimes Are Not Observed
title: A Generalized Framework for Estimating Customer Lifetime Value When Customer Lifetimes Are Not Observed
authors: Phillip E. Pfeifer, Robert L. Carraway

category: MarTech & Customer Analytics Economics > Churn Prediction & Retention Marketing

name: Aggregate Advertising Models: The State of the Art
title: Aggregate Advertising Models: The State of the Art
description: THE foundational paper for marketing mix modeling. Establishes diminishing returns, carryover effects, and competitive interactions—the theoretical underpinning of all modern MMM systems.

name: Sustained Spending and Persistent Response: A New Look at Long-Term Marketing Profitability
title: Sustained Spending and Persistent Response: A New Look at Long-Term Marketing Profitability
authors: Marnik G. Dekimpe, Dominique M. Hanssens

title: Return on Marketing Investment (ROMI): Definition, Uses, and Challenges

title: Data-driven Multi-touch Attribution Models

name: The Effectiveness of Triggered Email Marketing in Addressing Browse Abandonments
title: The Effectiveness of Triggered Email Marketing in Addressing Browse Abandonments

name: Personalization versus Privacy: An Empirical Examination of the Online Consumer's Dilemma
title: Personalization versus Privacy: An Empirical Examination of the Online Consumer's Dilemma

name: The Personalization-Privacy Paradox in the Attention Economy
title: The Personalization-Privacy Paradox in the Attention Economy
description: Connects personalization-privacy trade-offs to the attention economy framework. Shows how platform incentives and attention scarcity affect consumer privacy decisions and personalization acceptance.

name: Customization of Online Advertising: The Role of Intrusiveness
title: Customization of Online Advertising: The Role of Intrusiveness

name: Decomposing the Promotional Revenue Bump for Loyalty Program Members versus Nonmembers
title: Decomposing the Promotional Revenue Bump for Loyalty Program Members versus Nonmembers
authors: Harald J. van Heerde, Peter S.H. Leeflang, Dick R. Wittink

title: The Long-Term Impact of Loyalty Programs on Consumer Purchase Behavior and Loyalty

name: Do Customer Loyalty Programs Really Work?
title: Do Customer Loyalty Programs Really Work?

name: Generative AI for Economic Research: Use Cases and Implications for Economists
title: Generative AI for Economic Research: Use Cases and Implications for Economists

title: Large Language Models: A Primer for Economists

title: How to Learn and Teach Economics with Large Language Models

title: Large Language Models as Simulated Economic Agents: What Can We Learn from Homo Silicus?
authors: John J. Horton, Apostolos Filippas, Benjamin S. Manning
description: Foundational paper introducing homo silicus—using LLMs as implicit computational models of humans. Replicates classic experiments from Charness & Rabin (2002), Kahneman et al. (1986), finding qualitatively similar results. Published in ACM EC'24.
category: AI for Economic Research > Synthetic Agents & Homo Silicus

name: Automated Social Science: Language Models as Scientist and Subjects
title: Automated Social Science: Language Models as Scientist and Subjects
authors: Benjamin S. Manning, Kehang Zhu, John J. Horton
description: NBER Working Paper 32381. Framework using LLMs to both generate research hypotheses and serve as experimental subjects.
category: AI for Economic Research > Synthetic Agents & Homo Silicus

name: Out of One, Many: Using Language Models to Simulate Human Samples
title: Out of One, Many: Using Language Models to Simulate Human Samples
authors: Lisa P. Argyle, Ethan C. Busby, Nancy Fulda, Joshua R. Gubler, Christopher Rytting, David Wingate
description: Introduces 'silicon sampling'—conditioning LLMs with demographic backstories to simulate subpopulation opinions. Develops 'algorithmic fidelity' concept measuring simulation accuracy. Published in Political Analysis.
category: AI for Economic Research > Synthetic Agents & Homo Silicus

name: Synthetic Replacements for Human Survey Data? The Perils of Large Language Models
title: Synthetic Replacements for Human Survey Data? The Perils of Large Language Models
authors: James Bisbee, Joshua D. Clinton, Cassy Dorff, Brenton Kenkel, Jennifer Larson
description: Critical validation study: 48% of regression coefficients differ significantly from human data; 32% sign flips. Important cautionary findings.
category: AI for Economic Research > Synthetic Agents & Homo Silicus

name: Large Language Models Empowered Agent-based Modeling and Simulation: A Survey and Perspectives
title: Large Language Models Empowered Agent-based Modeling and Simulation: A Survey and Perspectives
authors: Chen Gao, Xiaochong Lan, Nian Li, Yuan Yuan, Jingtao Ding, Zhilun Zhou, Fengli Xu, Yong Li
description: Comprehensive survey covering agent design, environment construction, and personalization for LLM-based simulations. Published in Nature Humanities and Social Sciences Communications.
category: AI for Economic Research > Synthetic Agents & Homo Silicus

name: Machine Learning: An Applied Econometric Approach
title: Machine Learning: An Applied Econometric Approach
description: THE foundational paper explaining ML's role in economics: ML solves prediction problems while economics focuses on parameter estimation. Over 1,500 citations. Published in Journal of Economic Perspectives.
category: AI for Economic Research > ML Methods for Economists

name: Machine Learning Methods That Economists Should Know About
title: Machine Learning Methods That Economists Should Know About
description: Comprehensive review including supervised/unsupervised learning, matrix completion, and ML-econometrics methods. Published in Annual Review of Economics.
category: AI for Economic Research > ML Methods for Economists

name: Deep Learning for Economists
title: Deep Learning for Economists
description: Comprehensive tutorial on classifiers, regression models, generative AI, and embedding models with demo notebooks. Published in Journal of Economic Literature. Companion site: econdl.github.io
category: AI for Economic Research > ML Methods for Economists

name: Machine Learning as a Tool for Hypothesis Generation
title: Machine Learning as a Tool for Hypothesis Generation
description: Systematic ML procedure for generating novel hypotheses. Application: defendant mugshots explain ~50% of predictable variation in judge decisions. Published in Quarterly Journal of Economics.
category: AI for Economic Research > ML Methods for Economists

name: Recursive Partitioning for Heterogeneous Causal Effects
title: Recursive Partitioning for Heterogeneous Causal Effects
description: Introduces 'honest' causal trees using sample splitting. Published in PNAS.
category: AI for Economic Research > Causal Machine Learning

name: Generalized Random Forests
title: Generalized Random Forests
authors: Susan Athey, Julie Tibshirani, Stefan Wager
description: Framework extending random forests to solve local moment equations. Published in Annals of Statistics.
category: AI for Economic Research > Causal Machine Learning

name: Text as Data
title: Text as Data
authors: Matthew Gentzkow, Bryan Kelly, Matt Taddy
description: THE seminal survey providing introduction to text-as-data methods in economics. Published in Journal of Economic Literature.
category: AI for Economic Research > Text as Data

name: Measuring Group Differences in High-Dimensional Choices: Method and Application to Congressional Speech
title: Measuring Group Differences in High-Dimensional Choices: Method and Application to Congressional Speech
authors: Matthew Gentzkow, Jesse M. Shapiro, Matt Taddy
description: ML methodology for measuring partisanship in congressional speech (1873-2016). Published in Econometrica.
category: AI for Economic Research > Text as Data

name: Text Algorithms in Economics
title: Text Algorithms in Economics
description: Overview covering word embeddings, topic models, and transformers for economics research. Published in Annual Review of Economics.
category: AI for Economic Research > Text as Data

name: Measuring Economic Growth from Outer Space
title: Measuring Economic Growth from Outer Space
authors: J. Vernon Henderson, Adam Storeygard, David N. Weil
description: Foundational paper using nighttime lights to proxy GDP. For poor-data countries, optimal growth estimate weights lights equally with official statistics. Published in American Economic Review.
category: AI for Economic Research > Satellite Imagery & Computer Vision

name: Combining Satellite Imagery and Machine Learning to Predict Poverty
title: Combining Satellite Imagery and Machine Learning to Predict Poverty
authors: Neal Jean, Marshall Burke, Michael Xie, W. Matthew Davis, David B. Lobell, Stefano Ermon
description: Landmark study: CNNs trained on satellite imagery explain 75% of variation in local economic outcomes across 5 African countries. Published in Science.
category: AI for Economic Research > Satellite Imagery & Computer Vision

name: Using Publicly Available Satellite Imagery and Deep Learning to Understand Economic Well-Being in Africa
title: Using Publicly Available Satellite Imagery and Deep Learning to Understand Economic Well-Being in Africa
authors: Christopher Yeh, Anthony Perez, Anne Driscoll, George Azzari, Zhongyi Tang, David Lobell, Stefano Ermon, Marshall Burke
description: Models predict 70% of variation in village wealth across held-out African countries. Published in Nature Communications.
category: AI for Economic Research > Satellite Imagery & Computer Vision

name: Using Deep Learning and Google Street View to Estimate the Demographic Makeup of Neighborhoods across the United States
title: Using Deep Learning and Google Street View to Estimate the Demographic Makeup of Neighborhoods across the United States
authors: Timnit Gebru, Jonathan Krause, Yilun Wang, Duyun Chen, Jia Deng, Erez Lieberman Aiden, Li Fei-Fei
description: Car detection infers income, race, voting patterns from 50M Google Street View images. Published in PNAS.
category: AI for Economic Research > Satellite Imagery & Computer Vision

name: Agent-Based Computational Economics: A Constructive Approach to Economic Theory
title: Agent-Based Computational Economics: A Constructive Approach to Economic Theory
description: Foundational survey establishing ACE methodology. Defines agent-based computational economics as the computational study of economies modeled as evolving systems of autonomous interacting agents. Published in Handbook of Computational Economics Vol. 2.

name: Agent-Based Modeling in Economics and Finance: Past, Present, and Future
title: Agent-Based Modeling in Economics and Finance: Past, Present, and Future
description: Definitive 90-page survey in Journal of Economic Literature reviewing 30 years of ABM in economics. Covers finance, industrial organization, macroeconomics, and policy applications. Essential reading for the field.

name: Artificial Economic Life: A Simple Model of a Stockmarket
title: Artificial Economic Life: A Simple Model of a Stockmarket
authors: W. Brian Arthur, John H. Holland, Blake LeBaron, Richard Palmer, Paul Tayler
description: The Santa Fe Artificial Stock Market—foundational heterogeneous agent financial model. Shows how bubbles and crashes emerge from adaptive learning traders. Seminal work in agent-based finance.

name: The Economy Needs Agent-Based Modelling
title: The Economy Needs Agent-Based Modelling
description: Nature commentary arguing for ABM in economic policy. Critiques DSGE models' failure to predict 2008 crisis; calls for bottom-up agent-based approaches to model systemic risk.

name: Leverage Causes Fat Tails and Clustered Volatility
title: Leverage Causes Fat Tails and Clustered Volatility
authors: Stefan Thurner, J. Doyne Farmer, John Geanakoplos
description: Agent-based explanation of financial market fat tails and volatility clustering. Shows leveraged agents create price fluctuations 10x larger than fundamentals. Published in Quantitative Finance.

name: Mesa: An Agent-Based Modeling Framework
title: Mesa: An Agent-Based Modeling Framework
authors: Jackie Kazil, David Masad, Andrew Crooks
description: Introduces Mesa, the leading open-source Python ABM framework. Describes modular architecture with spatial grids, agent schedulers, and data collection. Published in JOSS.

name: Econ-ARK and HARK: Open-Source Tools for Computational Economics
title: Econ-ARK and HARK: Open-Source Tools for Computational Economics
authors: Christopher D. Carroll, Alexander M. Kaufman, Jacqueline L. Kazil, Nathan M. Palmer, Matthew N. White
description: Describes Econ-ARK ecosystem and HARK toolkit for heterogeneous agent modeling. NumFOCUS-sponsored project implementing Aiyagari, buffer-stock, and lifecycle models.

name: A Standard Protocol for Describing Individual-Based and Agent-Based Models
title: A Standard Protocol for Describing Individual-Based and Agent-Based Models
authors: Volker Grimm, Uta Berger, Finn Bastiansen, Sigrunn Eliassen, Vincent Ginot, Jarl Giske, John Goss-Custard, Tamara Grand, Simone K. Heinz, Geir Huse, Andreas Huth, Jane U. Jepsen, Christian Jørgensen, Wolf M. Mooij, Birgit Müller, Guy Pe'er, Cyril Piou, Steven F. Railsback, Andrew M. Robbins, Martha M. Robbins, Eva Rossmanith, Nadja Rüger, Espen Strand, Sami Souissi, Richard A. Stillman, Rune Vabø, Ute Visser, Donald L. DeAngelis
description: The ODD (Overview, Design concepts, Details) protocol for describing ABMs. Standard framework for model documentation adopted across ecology and social simulation.

name: Modeling Tabular Data using Conditional GAN
title: Modeling Tabular Data using Conditional GAN
authors: Lei Xu, Maria Skoularidou, Alfredo Cuesta-Infante, Kalyan Veeramachaneni
description: Introduces CTGAN using mode-specific normalization and conditional generator for tabular data synthesis. Handles mixed discrete/continuous columns. Published at NeurIPS.
category: Simulation & Synthetic Data > Synthetic Data Generation & Privacy

name: DataSynthesizer: Privacy-Preserving Synthetic Datasets
title: DataSynthesizer: Privacy-Preserving Synthetic Datasets
authors: Haoyue Ping, Julia Stoyanovich, Bill Howe
description: Introduces DataSynthesizer for generating synthetic data with differential privacy using Bayesian networks. Three modes: random, independent attributes, and correlated attributes.
category: Simulation & Synthetic Data > Synthetic Data Generation & Privacy

name: synthpop: Bespoke Creation of Synthetic Data in R
title: synthpop: Bespoke Creation of Synthetic Data in R
authors: Beata Nowok, Gillian M. Raab, Chris Dibben
description: Introduces synthpop R package using CART-based synthesis. Produces realistic synthetic data preserving statistical relationships. Published in Journal of Statistical Software.
category: Simulation & Synthetic Data > Synthetic Data Generation & Privacy

name: The Synthetic Data Vault
title: The Synthetic Data Vault
authors: Neha Patki, Roy Wedge, Kalyan Veeramachaneni
description: Introduces SDV system for synthesizing relational databases while preserving referential integrity. Uses copulas and deep learning for multi-table synthesis.
category: Simulation & Synthetic Data > Synthetic Data Generation & Privacy

name: Anonymeter: A Python Library for Privacy Risk Assessment
title: Anonymeter: A Python Library for Privacy Risk Assessment
authors: Lucas Giomi, Eleonora Botta, Marco Esposito, Julien Herzen, Michael Grossniklaus
description: Framework for GDPR-aligned privacy risk quantification. Measures singling out, linkability, and inference risks for synthetic datasets.
category: Simulation & Synthetic Data > Synthetic Data Generation & Privacy

name: The AI Economist: Taxation Policy Design via Two-Level Deep Reinforcement Learning
title: The AI Economist: Taxation Policy Design via Two-Level Deep Reinforcement Learning
authors: Stephan Zheng, Alexander Trott, Sunil Srinivasa, David C. Parkes, Richard Socher
description: Two-level RL for optimal taxation: agents optimize labor/trade, social planner optimizes tax policy. Finds policies outperforming baselines by 16% on equality-productivity. Published in Science Advances.
category: Simulation & Synthetic Data > Mechanism Design & Reinforcement Learning

name: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning in Sequential Social Dilemmas
title: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning in Sequential Social Dilemmas
authors: Joel Z. Leibo, Vinicius Zambaldi, Marc Lanctot, Janusz Marecki, Thore Graepel
description: Foundational work on multi-agent RL in games with mixed cooperative/competitive incentives. Introduces sequential social dilemmas; shows cooperation emergence depends on environment structure.
category: Simulation & Synthetic Data > Mechanism Design & Reinforcement Learning

name: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Optimal Execution
title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Optimal Execution
authors: Yong Lin, Zhe Feng, Lihong Li, Marcus Zahradka, Harikrishna Narasimhan, David C. Parkes
description: Applies deep RL to optimal order execution problem. Learns execution policies that outperform TWAP/VWAP benchmarks on real market data.
category: Simulation & Synthetic Data > Mechanism Design & Reinforcement Learning

name: Discovering Algorithmic Pricing in Practice: A Framework for Learning-Based Collusion
title: Discovering Algorithmic Pricing in Practice: A Framework for Learning-Based Collusion
authors: Timo Becker, Zhi Chen, Silvio Micali, Zhiyi Huang
description: Studies emergence of tacit collusion in RL-based pricing algorithms. Shows Q-learning agents can learn supra-competitive prices without explicit coordination.
category: Simulation & Synthetic Data > Mechanism Design & Reinforcement Learning

name: ABIDES: Towards High-Fidelity Multi-Agent Market Simulation
title: ABIDES: Towards High-Fidelity Multi-Agent Market Simulation
authors: David Byrd, Maria Hybinette, Tucker Hybinette Balch
description: Introduces ABIDES (Agent-Based Interactive Discrete Event Simulation) from JPMorgan. NASDAQ-like exchange with ZI, momentum, and market maker agents. Published at AAMAS.
category: Simulation & Synthetic Data > Market Microstructure Simulation

name: Get Real: Realism Metrics for Robust Limit Order Book Market Simulations
title: Get Real: Realism Metrics for Robust Limit Order Book Market Simulations
authors: Svitlana Vyetrenko, David Byrd, Nick Petosa, Mahmoud Mahfouz, Danial Dervovic, Manuela Veloso, Tucker Hybinette Balch
description: Establishes stylized facts benchmarks for evaluating LOB simulation realism. Proposes metrics for fat tails, volatility clustering, and bid-ask spread dynamics.
category: Simulation & Synthetic Data > Market Microstructure Simulation

name: Limit Order Book Simulation Methods: A Review
title: Limit Order Book Simulation Methods: A Review
authors: Rama Cont, Arseniy Kukanov, Sasha Stoikov
description: Comprehensive review of LOB simulation methods: order flow models, agent-based approaches, and deep learning. Covers validation metrics and calibration techniques.
category: Simulation & Synthetic Data > Market Microstructure Simulation

name: AuctionGym: Simulating Online Advertising Auctions
title: AuctionGym: Simulating Online Advertising Auctions
authors: Martin Mladenov, Sloan Nietert, Kunhe Yang, Aranyak Mehta, Christos Tzamos, Craig Boutilier
description: Amazon's ad auction simulator for training RL bidding agents. Supports first/second-price auctions with realistic features. Best Paper at AdKDD 2022.
category: Simulation & Synthetic Data > Market Microstructure Simulation

name: A Proof for the Queuing Formula: L = λW
title: A Proof for the Queuing Formula: L = λW
description: THE foundational result of queueing theory. Little's Law states that the long-run average number of customers (L) equals the arrival rate (λ) times the average time spent (W). Remarkably simple, distribution-free, and universally applicable.
category: Queueing Theory & Operations > Foundational Queueing Theory

name: The Theory of Probabilities and Telephone Conversations
title: The Theory of Probabilities and Telephone Conversations
description: The founding paper of queueing theory. Erlang developed formulas for telephone exchange capacity planning that are still used today. Introduced the Erlang B (blocking) and Erlang C (waiting) formulas.
category: Queueing Theory & Operations > Foundational Queueing Theory

name: Jobshop-Like Queueing Systems
title: Jobshop-Like Queueing Systems
description: Proved that open queueing networks with Poisson arrivals and exponential service have product-form steady-state distributions. This 'Jackson network' result enables tractable analysis of complex multi-stage systems.
category: Queueing Theory & Operations > Foundational Queueing Theory

name: The Single Server Queue in Heavy Traffic
title: The Single Server Queue in Heavy Traffic
description: Derived the heavy traffic approximation for GI/G/1 queues. Kingman's formula states that mean wait ≈ (ρ/(1-ρ)) × (c²ₐ + c²ₛ)/2 × μ⁻¹, where c² are squared coefficients of variation. Essential for capacity planning.
category: Queueing Theory & Operations > Foundational Queueing Theory

name: The Output of a Queuing System
title: The Output of a Queuing System
description: Burke's Theorem: the departure process from an M/M/c queue in steady state is Poisson with the same rate as arrivals. Enables analysis of tandem queues and feeds into Jackson network theory.
category: Queueing Theory & Operations > Foundational Queueing Theory

name: Queues with Negative Arrivals
title: Queues with Negative Arrivals
description: Introduced G-networks with 'negative customers' that remove positive customers from queues. Extended product-form solutions to systems with deletions, enabling models of caches, memory, and biological systems.
category: Queueing Theory & Operations > Foundational Queueing Theory

name: Queueing-Theoretic Approach to Ride-Sharing
title: Queueing-Theoretic Approach to Ride-Sharing
authors: Siddhartha Banerjee, Daniel Freund, Thodoris Lykouris
description: Develops a spatial queueing model for ride-sharing platforms. Analyzes optimal dispatching, pricing, and the value of pooling. Shows that simple policies can achieve near-optimal performance.

name: Dynamic Spatial Matching
title: Dynamic Spatial Matching
authors: Itai Ashlagi, Maximilien Burq, Patrick Jaillet, Vahideh Manshadi
description: Studies dynamic matching in spatial markets like ride-sharing. Analyzes the trade-off between matching quickly (reducing wait) and matching well (reducing travel distance). Characterizes optimal patience levels.

name: Empty-Car Routing in Ridesharing Systems
title: Empty-Car Routing in Ridesharing Systems
description: Addresses repositioning of empty vehicles in ride-sharing. Uses fluid model to derive optimal rebalancing policies. Shows significant improvements over reactive dispatching.

name: Heavy Traffic Limits for Queues with Many Exponential Servers
title: Heavy Traffic Limits for Queues with Many Exponential Servers
description: Introduced the Halfin-Whitt regime (QED: Quality and Efficiency Driven) for many-server queues. Shows that staffing with n = λ/μ + β√(λ/μ) servers balances efficiency and service quality. Foundation for modern call center staffing.
category: Queueing Theory & Operations > Call Centers & Service Operations

name: Staffing of Time-Varying Queues to Achieve Time-Stable Performance
title: Staffing of Time-Varying Queues to Achieve Time-Stable Performance
authors: Avishai Mandelbaum, William Massey, Martin Reiman
description: Addresses staffing when arrivals vary over time (daily patterns). Develops modified offered load (MOL) approach that adapts staffing to time-varying demand while maintaining stable service levels.
category: Queueing Theory & Operations > Call Centers & Service Operations

name: Dynamic Call Center Routing
title: Dynamic Call Center Routing
description: Analyzes routing policies in call centers with multiple customer types and agent skills. Compares static versus dynamic policies and characterizes when sophisticated routing provides value.
category: Queueing Theory & Operations > Call Centers & Service Operations

name: Queueing Models of Call Centers: An Introduction
title: Queueing Models of Call Centers: An Introduction
description: Accessible introduction to queueing models for call centers. Covers Erlang formulas, abandonment, skill-based routing, and software tools. Good starting point for practitioners.
category: Queueing Theory & Operations > Call Centers & Service Operations

name: The Tail at Scale
title: The Tail at Scale
description: Seminal paper on latency management in large-scale systems. Shows how tail latencies compound in distributed systems and presents techniques (hedged requests, tied requests, micro-partitioning) to tame them.
category: Queueing Theory & Operations > Cloud & Server Systems

name: Large-scale Cluster Management at Google with Borg
title: Large-scale Cluster Management at Google with Borg
description: Describes Google's Borg system for cluster management. Covers bin packing, priority queues, admission control, and resource allocation. Foundational for understanding Kubernetes and modern orchestration.
category: Queueing Theory & Operations > Cloud & Server Systems

name: The Power of Two Choices in Randomized Load Balancing
title: The Power of Two Choices in Randomized Load Balancing
description: Shows that choosing the least loaded of TWO random servers (instead of one) exponentially reduces maximum queue length. This 'power of two choices' principle revolutionized load balancing in distributed systems.
category: Queueing Theory & Operations > Cloud & Server Systems

name: Analysis of Join-the-Shortest-Queue Routing
title: Analysis of Join-the-Shortest-Queue Routing
description: Provides tight analysis of join-the-shortest-queue (JSQ) policy in heterogeneous server systems. Characterizes when JSQ is optimal and when it can be significantly improved.
category: Queueing Theory & Operations > Cloud & Server Systems

name: Delay Tails and Service Levels in Multi-Server Service Systems
title: Delay Tails and Service Levels in Multi-Server Service Systems
description: Studies tail behavior of delays in multi-server queues. Shows how to predict and manage service level agreements (SLAs) based on delay tail probabilities.
category: Queueing Theory & Operations > Cloud & Server Systems

name: Queueing Models for Healthcare Operations
title: Queueing Models for Healthcare Operations
description: Comprehensive survey of queueing applications in healthcare. Covers emergency departments, operating rooms, bed management, appointment scheduling, and staffing. Essential reference for healthcare operations.

name: Managing Patient Flow in Hospital Networks
title: Managing Patient Flow in Hospital Networks
authors: Santiago Balseiro, Dragos Florin Ciocan, Adam Elmachtoub
description: Studies patient routing across hospital networks. Develops fluid models for patient flow and proposes routing policies that balance load across hospitals. Addresses the COVID-19 surge capacity problem.

name: Emergency Department Staffing
title: Emergency Department Staffing
authors: Linda Green, Sergei Savin, Ben Wang
description: Applies queueing theory to emergency department staffing. Shows how time-varying demand and service times affect optimal staffing. Develops practical staffing algorithms used by real EDs.

name: Operating Room Scheduling
title: Operating Room Scheduling
authors: Brian Denton, James Viapiano, Andrea Vogl
description: Studies stochastic scheduling of surgical cases. Develops robust scheduling methods that account for surgery duration uncertainty. Shows trade-offs between OR utilization and overtime.

name: Patient Flow in Hospitals: A Data-Driven Approach
title: Patient Flow in Hospitals: A Data-Driven Approach
description: Uses hospital data to validate and calibrate queueing models. Shows how to fit time-varying arrival rates, service times, and abandonment. Bridges theory and practice in healthcare queueing.
